title: Annotations

---

An [`AnnotationSet`](`dascore.core.annotations.AnnotationSet`) records where things are in a patch's dimensions: phase picks, boxes around noise, vehicle tracks, outlines of a region. It is a dataframe first. A picker's output is one table, and the same set can grow into grouped events, paths and polygons without changing what it already holds.

Annotations describe data but never hold it. They are stated in coordinates, not sample indices, so they stay valid when the data is decimated, trimmed or re-chunked.

# The model

A set has three parts:

- **annotations**: one row per located thing. For each dimension a row states a single value (`time`), a half-open range (`time_min`, `time_max`), or nothing, in which case it spans that dimension. A row stating only `time` is an instant across the whole fiber.
- **features**: what rows compose. Every row belongs to one feature, named by its `feature_id`; a row with none is its own feature. A feature is a `group` (unordered, the default), a `path` (vertices ordered by `seq`), or a `polygon` (rings ordered by `seq`, `ring` 0 outside, holes after). `part` numbers the pieces of a multipart shape.
- **bases**: named curves, such as a line or a moveout, that a path is drawn from. A path may state only its basis and is sampled when needed.

Any other column, such as `phase`, `confidence` or `note`, is yours and is kept as written. Features hold no coordinates; their bounds come from their rows.

| time | distance_min | distance_max | phase | feature_id | reads as |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.01 | | | P | | an instant across the fiber |
| 0.01 | 650 | 750 | P | event_1 | a pick on a stretch, part of `event_1` |
| | 400 | 450 | | | a stretch of fiber at all times |

# Picks

A picker's output is a single table. [`AnnotationSet.from_patch`](`dascore.core.annotations.AnnotationSet.from_patch`) takes the dimensions from the patch and stamps its `acquisition_key` and `data_id`, so the set records which data it was made on.

```{python}
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd

import dascore as dc

patch = dc.get_example_patch("example_event_2")
picks = pd.DataFrame(
    {
        "time": [0.018, 0.010, 0.017, 0.052, 0.026, 0.045],
        "distance": [600.0, 700.0, 800.0, 600.0, 700.0, 800.0],
        "phase": ["P", "P", "P", "S", "S", "S"],
        "confidence": [0.9, 0.95, 0.8, 0.7, 0.9, 0.4],
    }
)
ann = dc.AnnotationSet.from_patch(patch, picks)
ann.annotations
```

A set of only annotations writes as one bare file, CSV or Parquet. The file holds the annotations table alone; Parquet also keeps the dimensions, while the set's attributes, such as `data_id`, need the directory form described under [Saving and loading](#saving-and-loading).

```{python}
folder = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
path = ann.io.to_parquet(folder / "picks.parquet")
assert dc.annotations(path).annotations.equals(ann.annotations)
```

# Building features

Picks become an event by sharing a `feature_id`. A `feature_id` naming no feature creates a group, so the picker never writes a features table:

```{python}
event = dc.AnnotationSet.from_patch(patch, picks.assign(feature_id="event_1"))
event.features
```

Builders return new sets. In [`add_path`](`dascore.core.annotations.AnnotationSet.add_path`) an array keyword is an annotations column, one value per vertex, and a scalar keyword is a features column:

```{python}
ann = event.add_path(
    "s_wave",
    time=[0.026, 0.06, 0.09],
    distance=[700.0, 580.0, 470.0],
    amplitude=[20.0, 12.0, 6.0],
    wave="S",
)
ann["s_wave"].kind, ann["s_wave"].extra
```

A path can also be drawn from a basis, given as a model or its document, and no vertices:

```{python}
line = {
    "object_type": "Line",
    "start": {"time": 0.01, "distance": 700.0},
    "end": {"time": 0.04, "distance": 900.0},
}
ann = ann.add_path("p_wave", basis=line, wave="P")
```

[`add_polygon`](`dascore.core.annotations.AnnotationSet.add_polygon`) takes rings, the outer ring first and then any holes, each a table of vertices in order. Closure is implied:

```{python}
outer = {"time": [0.06, 0.1, 0.1, 0.06], "distance": [400.0, 400.0, 450.0, 450.0]}
ann = ann.add_polygon("noise", rings=[outer], note="traffic")
ann
```

# Querying

[`select`](`dascore.core.annotations.AnnotationSet.select`) filters on columns of either table. A value matches, a list is membership, and a tuple is an inclusive range:

```{python}
confident_p = ann.select(phase="P", confidence=(0.85, None))
confident_p.annotations
```

[`overlapping`](`dascore.core.annotations.AnnotationSet.overlapping`) selects by location and keeps or drops each feature whole. Given a patch, it queries that patch's extent:

```{python}
early = ann.overlapping(time=(0.0, 0.02))
in_patch = ann.overlapping(patch.select(distance=(600, 800)))
[x.id for x in in_patch]
```

[`bounds`](`dascore.core.annotations.AnnotationSet.bounds`) gives each feature's extent, one row per feature:

```{python}
ann.bounds()
```

# Editing

[`update`](`dascore.core.annotations.AnnotationSet.update`) changes the columns of one feature or one annotation, and [`remove`](`dascore.core.annotations.AnnotationSet.remove`) drops one. [`merge`](`dascore.core.annotations.AnnotationSet.merge`) combines sets stated in the same dimensions, such as hand and automatic picks.

```{python}
ann = ann.update(feature="event_1", magnitude=1.2).remove(feature="noise")
```

# Plotting

[`ann.viz.plot`](`dascore.viz.annotations.plot`) draws every feature on an axis, putting dimensions where [`waterfall`](`dascore.viz.waterfall.waterfall`) puts them. Draw the patch first and the annotations over it. `color` may name a column, giving one color per value and a legend:

```{python}
ax = patch.viz.waterfall()
ax = ann.viz.plot(ax=ax, color="phase")
```

A pick is a marker, a path a line, a polygon a filled outline, and a row spanning one axis a line or band across it.

# Saving and loading

A set with features or bases is saved as a directory holding `attrs.json`, the annotations and features tables, and `bases.json`. [`dc.annotations`](`dascore.annotations`) reads it back, and also reads bare tables and collections of sets:

```{python}
directory = ann.io.save(folder / "event_1")
assert dc.annotations(directory) == ann
```
